subject: Television & Streaming
title: How Sitcoms Shaped America
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on How Sitcoms Shaped America.

hook.text: By 1960, the average American family watched over five hours of TV daily. Much of it was sitcoms.

buildup.text: Sitcoms taught unwritten rules: how families should talk, what homes should look like, who belonged.

discovery.text: Shows like Father Knows Best reinforced gender roles so effectively that sociologists studied them.

twist.text: But sitcoms also challenged norms. All in the Family tackled racism in 1971, shocking millions into conversation.

climax.text: The sitcom became America's mirror—sometimes flattering, sometimes painful, always impossible to ignore.

punchline.text: Half-hour comedies taught America who to be.

quiz.question: Which 1971 sitcom directly tackled racism and social issues?
